title: Birb performance workbench + adaptive controller — requirement register

authoredAt.note: Line numbers throughout are provenance at this commit, not identity. Sites are identified by their verbatim anchor string.

rules: A cheap-tier agent may TRANSCRIBE from this file and may not DECIDE. Anything absent here is not a licence to invent it.
No fixture, corpus, test, contract or default may treat a provenance:'unmeasured' value as fixed. Wave 4 unlocks them.
A field with no source renders its sentinel (see sentinelProtocol). Never 0, never a plausible default, never a value derived from intent.
A wave may add rows. Changing a comparator, a sentinel, a precedence order, or a provisional number's provenance is a gate decision recorded in docs/perf/gates/G<n>.md.
shipped-unvalidated is not measured. The live 55/58 family has never been validated against a working measurement.

forbiddenSubstitutes: bare null in a display slot
any value derived from intent rather than read from the live object
sentinelProtocol.stopCondition: GPU timer reporting reason 'no-context' is a wiring bug wearing a platform fact's clothes (the hardwareConcurrency/bloom trap). 'no-extension' is a legitimate platform fact.

resume.note: fires on HIDE, not on SHOW; adaptiveTier's own state.fpsSum/windowStart is not reset at all (GAP-5)

pausedIsNotAReset.rule: Paused measurements are marked invalid for adaptive decisions and RETAINED in the buffer and the export. They are never erased. 'Mark paused measurements invalid' is not 'discard them'.
pausedIsNotAReset.controllerRule: Percentiles fed to the controller are computed over valid===true only. Percentiles in the export state both counts.

exceptions: reducedMotionState is an accessibility preference and is outside this hierarchy: it wins for the decorative motion it gates, is never a performance lever, and performance never turns it on.
Emergency downshifts during severe sustained overload apply in Auto only, never over an active Manual/Benchmark lock.

requirements.verbatim: The adaptive manager uses three bundled tiers, 250 ms FPS samples and averages.
requirements.consequence: Tier 0->1 changes DPR 1.7->1.0, switches bloom off and reduces other effects together. Separate the controls.

requirements.verbatim: The averaging window is selected by the current tier.
requirements.consequence: At tier 1 a further downgrade waits the same four-second window used for recovery. Separate overload and recovery timers.

requirements.verbatim: Tier changes call renderer.setPixelRatio() directly; resize handling separately sizes the bloom targets.
requirements.consequence: Resizing while degraded, then restoring, can leave the scene target below the requested resolution. Route every quality/viewport change through one sizing function.
requirements.oracle: A6 (must fail on HEAD, per EXPECTED-RED)

requirements.verbatim: Bloom stats snapshot the scene before post-processing.
requirements.consequence: Show both scene and whole-frame totals.

requirements.verbatim: Background/environment transitions reset the frame sampler; the tier manager has separate accumulated state.
requirements.consequence: Add a coordinated reset so stale history does not cross loading, resume or resize boundaries.
requirements.detail: frameSampler.reset() fires at three sites (3489 construction, 5725 environment, 8763 hide); adaptiveTier's state.fpsSum/fpsCount/windowStart is reset at none.
requirements.oracle: resetTags enum coverage + trace corpus resume/scene-change traces

requirements.verbatim: Debug hooks expose bloom, lighting, stats and pinTier; there is no unpin method.
requirements.consequence: Reuse these capabilities behind a common settings API; add explicit Resume Auto and reset. setLighting/setBloom remain adapters.

requirements.verbatim: Three-finger QR overlays exist in sibling apps; no matching root dev-console integration was found.
requirements.consequence: Reuse the gesture recognition pattern, then wire the requested panel into root Birb. Do not assume the sibling overlay already controls this game.
requirements.evidence: grep for 'three-finger' in index.html returns nothing; the QR lives in gauntlet/src/ui/qr.js only

requirements.verbatim: Auto / Manual / Benchmark — Manual suspends Auto. Benchmark fixes seed, route, settings and sun; it does not adapt during a comparison. Resume Auto clears stale history.
requirements.notes: Benchmark MUST freeze the sun: the sun cycle is ten minutes long, so an A/B taken three minutes apart is confounded. Resume Auto emits the 'manual' reset tag.

requirements.verbatim: Target rate — 60 default; explicit 30 FPS battery/stability option with actual render pacing. Add 90/120 only after observed browser cadence and device testing justify them.
requirements.notes: 30 FPS row is DEFERRED (DEF-3) until a pacing mechanism is named; 90/120 likewise. Ships 60 only.

requirements.verbatim: Resolution — Absolute render-DPR slider, initially 0.85-2.0 in 0.05 steps, bounded by native DPR and a maximum pixel budget. Default ceiling stays 1.7 mobile. Show effective buffer dimensions and native-resolution percentage. Values above today's cap are experimental.
requirements.notes: Range and step are PRO-9. Commit resolution changes at intervals, not on every slider input (SM-6).

requirements.verbatim: Post quality — Off / quarter / half resolution. Independent shafts toggle and bloom strength slider. Strength is a look adjustment, not a promise of lower rendering cost.
requirements.notes: downscale is constructor-only today and setSize keeps no state, so a live setter needs new cached w/h/ratio state (P2.2).

requirements.verbatim: Weather, mist, decorative effects — Density sliders 0-100%; hide/skip work at zero. Preserve gameplay targets and collision geometry.
requirements.notes: Zero must SKIP THE DRAW, not zero a uniform. Sites T4, T6, T7/T8, T9, T10 write these per frame and must be routed.

requirements.verbatim: Surface detail — Existing baseline / simplified / richer experimental variant. Shader variants apply on release and are prepared outside active flight.
requirements.notes: The 'richer experimental' third option is DEFERRED (DEF-4). Ships baseline/simplified.

requirements.verbatim: Look — Exposure, atmosphere/mist strength, wind and existing bloom threshold. Display current values; retain per-biome baselines. Auto never changes these artistic choices.
requirements.notes: 'Auto never changes these' is a hard rule, not a preference: the controller's approved settings ranges exclude every Look control.
requirements.oracle: A10; trace corpus asserts no Look write from the policy

requirements.verbatim: Compare / export / reset — Fixed-view A/B, copy/download JSON including build, seed, device/browser, requested/effective values and timing. Version local presets; keep benchmark/manual locks session-scoped.
requirements.notes: 'including build' is SW-4. requested AND effective are both required — reporting only one is how a desync hides.

requirements.verbatim: Collect frame intervals in a fixed-size buffer. Time CPU simulation and render submission separately. Feature-detect optional GPU timer queries, read completed results on later frames, discard disjoint results and clean up queries. A timer around renderer.render() is not GPU execution time.
requirements.notes: Zero-allocation: the ring buffer must be structurally zero-alloc, not merely 'the same object' — exportIntervals() invites a parallel unbounded plain Array. GPU timer is probe-only (DEF-2).
requirements.oracle: P1.1 red-first suites: percentiles vs an independent reference over ~200 seeded arrays; a structural zero-alloc assertion; a GPU-timer suite over a fake GL context including a context-loss trace

requirements.verbatim: Start from a conservative last-known stable profile or today's baseline, with a short warm-up. Use a target budget B = 1000 / targetFPS. Evaluate one-second windows; initial overload rule: p95 interval >1.2xB or >5% missed-target frames for two windows. Severe sustained overload may take another step sooner. Tune these numbers on phones.
requirements.notes: 'last-known stable profile' is IN-SESSION only in this programme — persistence is DEF-1.

requirements.verbatim: Restore one small step only after 10-15 seconds of stability, with roughly 20% measured CPU/GPU work headroom where available. Hold for 2-3 seconds after ordinary adjustments. If an upgrade regresses, roll back and lengthen its retry cooldown. Delivered 60 FPS alone does not reveal spare GPU capacity on a 60 Hz display; without GPU timing use occasional bounded probes and learn from their result.
requirements.notes: The bounded probe is NOT deferred — it is what will actually run, since the GPU timer is exposed by neither Safari nor SwiftShader.

requirements.verbatim: Diagnose approximately: if pixel reduction helps, target pixel/effect cost; if CPU work dominates and DPR changes do little, target decorative update rates, allocations or submission overhead. Keep confidence low when measurements are ambiguous. Persist an action only if it helps beyond noise. Never reduce collision, input or flight simulation fidelity to conceal a rendering bottleneck.
requirements.notes: The 'never reduce' clause is absolute and is echoed in the precedence block.

requirements.verbatim: Prefer low visual loss: reduce shaft work, distant mist/weather coverage and post resolution; then reduce scene DPR in 0.05-0.10 steps. Reorder this list from device A/B evidence. Protect the bird, near silhouettes, contact cues and readable targets. Uniform intensity changes alone may leave the expensive shader work intact.
requirements.notes: The ORDER of the ladder is itself unmeasured and is reordered from Wave 4 / Experiment 1 evidence.

requirements.verbatim: Apply renderer, scene target and effect dimensions atomically. Round dimensions and enforce total pixel/memory ceilings. Commit resolution changes at intervals, not on every slider input; repeated reallocations can create the stalls being measured. Keep HTML controls at CSS resolution.
requirements.notes: Atomically = one function, one call: renderer.setPixelRatio + setSize + bloomPass.setSize + weather.setPixelRatio + camera.aspect. handleContextRestored routes through it too.

requirements.verbatim: Reset all relevant history after bounded, explicitly tagged loading/resume/resize events. Do not erase recurrent gameplay hitches. Continue observing throughout the session and back off upgrades when sustainable performance declines. Report 'sustained slowdown', not a claimed temperature measurement. Never silently change the user's FPS target.
requirements.notes: This is the reset-tag enum (RUL-1). 'paused' is NOT one of these tags — it is a validity state (RUL-2).
requirements.oracle: resetTags coverage; trace corpus resume + scene-change traces

requirements.verbatim: Observe and predict: record the current effective settings, frame-time distribution, available CPU/GPU timings, biome, gameplay state and recent load trend. Select one bounded adjustment and record its expected benefit and confidence.

Apply and verify: confirm the effective buffer sizes, effect activity or update rates actually changed. A slider value changing is not evidence that rendering work changed. Allow the settling period before scoring.
requirements.notes: This is A3/A4/A5 as a RUNTIME check, not just a harness check.

requirements.verbatim: Evaluate: compare equal-duration windows in comparable gameplay conditions. A flight into a quieter area must not be credited to the adjustment. Mark changing scenes, unavailable evidence or differences within measured noise as inconclusive. Use controlled replay to establish causality during development; live observations provide weaker evidence.
requirements.notes: G3b rules on this by inspection — no fixture supplies it. Scene-change and input-heavy windows must be marked inconclusive, not credited.

requirements.verbatim: Keep or roll back: retain a quality reduction only when it provides a useful, measurable performance benefit, or is a temporary emergency measure pending evaluation. Retain a quality increase only when frame pacing and headroom remain within budget. Roll back ineffective reductions and failed upgrades; an inconclusive probe returns to the prior stable state once safe. Emergency recovery takes priority while severe overload persists.

Learn: maintain a small action history with predicted versus observed benefit, confidence, failed probes and cooldowns. Prefer actions with demonstrated benefit and low visual cost. Scope persisted summaries to build/settings schema, browser/device capability profile and biome; age out stale evidence, bound storage and revalidate after updates. Do not require a unique device fingerprint.
requirements.notes: PERSISTENCE IS DEFERRED (DEF-1). In-session action history ships. perf-learning.js gets its OWN authored test suite — three designs assigned the privacy deny-list, entry cap and age-out to a module with no test file.

requirements.verbatim: Evaluate the evaluator: track adjustment frequency, reversals, time outside budget, time spent unnecessarily degraded, prediction error and recovery time. Excessive oscillation or repeated ineffective actions disables exploratory upgrades and selects the last stable profile while protective downshifts remain active. A stable frame rate with permanently poor quality is not success: schedule occasional safe recovery probes.
requirements.notes: evaluateOscillation(tierChangeLog) is a property of the CHANGE LOG and must be a separate signature from the interval maths — a single-signature contract ships it as a hardcoded true. 'Stuck quality' (30s stable-but-degraded must produce a bounded probe) is a required trace.

requirements.summary: Per-change protocol: hypothesis and success gate -> fixed-build baseline -> change one factor -> matched A/B or A/B/A -> inspect timing, gameplay and visual evidence -> revise or revert -> rerun the affected gates. Final validation uses different routes and devices from those used to tune.

Every retained change carries an evidence record: hypothesis, build/settings/seed, device/browser, warm/cold state, repeated results and variability, observed visual tradeoff, decision, next unresolved issue.
requirements.notes: 'build' here is SW-4's build identity. Cold-start is recorded separately from warmed performance.

requirements.summary: Deterministic trace regressions for each controller failure found: slowdowns, recovery, missing/disjoint GPU queries, scene changes, misleading FPS plateaus, stuck quality settings and measurement overhead. Require bounded response, eventual recovery when capacity returns, correct rollback and freedom from persistent oscillation. Measure with telemetry and the panel both enabled and disabled.
requirements.notes: The corpus MUST be a CAPACITY MODEL, not a recorded interval array: each sample carries the sustainable frame cost at each setting and the driver synthesises dtMs from the controller's current profile. A fixed replay cannot depict recovery-when-capacity-returns or a failed upgrade probe, because the trace does not respond to the decision — and both are named required regressions. Traces are written in the FIXTURE SCHEMA so a device-observed failure becomes a regression by file copy.

requirements.summary: Bounded work: initially three candidate revisions per experiment. Stop when the gates pass with a visible benefit, or when repeated runs show no useful gain. Reopening needs new evidence or an explicit budget decision.

requirements.verbatim: Find the cost of today's realism. Fixed route, independently toggle ground detail, atmosphere, water, shafts, bloom, weather and ribbons. Repeat at two DPRs.
requirements.decisionRule: Rank visible benefit against p95 GPU/CPU cost; record interactions. Low draw-call counts do not prove cheap fragment shading.
requirements.notes: setFeature toggles must be run through tools/birb-modes.mjs with everything off, against the plan's own 'preserve gameplay targets and collision geometry'.

requirements.verbatim: Image stability before more effects. Compare current DPR 1.7 against slightly lower DPR with a bounded FXAA-style composite option; separately test low-sample target MSAA. Fade procedural microdetail below pixel scale.
requirements.notes: No mechanism exists anywhere in the repo. Needs a device-measured headroom figure as its stated budget. Do not add TAA/upscaling machinery first.

requirements.verbatim: Compute versus texture lookup. Compare current procedural noise against a small shared mipmapped noise/material atlas; precompute static terms where sensible.
requirements.notes: Zero production assets is a house rule for the siblings but not for root Birb; even so this is an asset-pipeline question and is Wave 6, one at a time.

requirements.verbatim: Spend detail where it is visible. Improve one bird/near-tree/waterfall material and silhouette; use screen-size thresholds for cosmetic detail.
requirements.notes: Avoid multiplying instanced batches or restoring previously rejected global sectors without evidence (DEF-7).

requirements.verbatim: Protect sustained smoothness. Profile allocations, first-use shader compilation and periodic decorative updates.
requirements.decisionRule: Remove actual spikes; stagger only noncritical work.
requirements.notes: The one evidence class that survives software rendering — allocation and compilation spikes are visible under SwiftShader in a way frame rate is not.

requirements.verbatim: Measurements and workbench: roughly 1-2 engineering days. Extend src/game/frame-metrics.js; add src/ui/dev-quality-panel.js and a settings API; correct whole-frame stats and sizing. Existing setLighting/setBloom hooks remain adapters. Make requested and effective settings agree after orientation changes and context recovery.

Controller: original estimate roughly 1-2 days for the basic policy. Extract it from index.html into src/game/adaptive-quality.js; split effect controls in src/effects/bloom-pass.js. Include the mandatory runtime evaluation, rollback and bounded learning loop. Test recorded/synthetic timing traces for overload, recovery, oscillation, absent GPU timers, manual->auto, resume and unsuccessful probes. A fake clock makes the policy tests cheap.
requirements.notes: createAdaptiveQuality({ apply, now, ... }) — imports nothing, side effects injected. Anything touching renderer directly stops npm test being an oracle for it and makes every task on it Opus work.

requirements.verbatim: Envelope experiments: roughly 1-2 days plus device access. Extend tools/birb-shot.mjs, birb-sheet.mjs and birb-modes.mjs with a seeded flight route and JSON performance capture. Change one thing at a time; rerun promising combinations.
requirements.notes: Blocked by evidence/device/manifest.json (Wave 4 hard stop).

requirements.verbatim: p95 frame interval <=18.5 ms
requirements.notes: Percentile convention MUST be pinned once (nearest-rank vs interpolated) and shared: the value the controller fires on and the value the acceptance gate scores must be computed by the same module, or the loop is closed against itself.

requirements.verbatim: <1% intervals >25 ms on the repeatable route
no recurring unexplained >50 ms spikes
no persistent quality oscillation after settling
requirements.notes: A property of the tier CHANGE LOG, not of the interval buffer. Separate signature, or it ships as a hardcoded true.

requirements.summary: A build identity literal exists: const BIRB_BUILD = '<same string as sw.js CACHE_VERSION>'. No build step (House Rule 5), so it is a literal.
A unit test asserts BIRB_BUILD === CACHE_VERSION by reading index.html and sw.js as TEXT (no browser, no import), so it runs under node --test against the tracked three stub with no install step.
The same test asserts CORE_ASSETS covers src/**/*.js on disk, minus an explicit commented allow-list of deliberate omissions. THIS is the row that makes sw.js owned.

currentState.note: the omission is CORRECT — it is unwired legacy kept as reference. Do not 'fix' it.

requirements.summary: The export carries build: { requested: BIRB_BUILD, serving: <string|null>, stale: requested !== serving }. serving is read page-side via caches.keys() -> birb-core-<CACHE_VERSION>, or a postMessage to navigator.serviceWorker.controller; Wave 2 picks one and states which. No SW registered => serving is the sentinel with reason 'not-applicable' and stale is false — absence of a service worker is not staleness.
requirements.why: staleWhileRevalidate serves the CACHED module first, so a device session's first run executes the PREVIOUS build's src/** against the new index.html. Every number from that session is attributed to a build that was not running.

requirements.summary: stale === true renders a visible panel warning and is recorded in every evidence export. A device number carrying stale:true is DISCARDED, not adjusted.
Assertion A12 covers SW-4 and SW-5.

requirements.ruling: The reset-tag enum is closed: {load, resume, resize, orientation, contextRestore, environment, manual}. An untagged reset is a contract violation. Resets are coordinated (sampler + controller accumulator + percentile buffer, one call, one tag) and clear only the adaptive decision windows — never the action history, the evidence record or the recurrent-hitch log.

'paused' is a VALIDITY STATE, not a reset tag. Paused measurements are marked invalid for adaptive decisions and RETAINED in the buffer and the export. Erasing them means the resume spike can never be studied and the controller learns nothing about a boundary it crosses every session.

THE PANEL AND THE GESTURE REGISTER ON THE PRODUCTION PATH, NOT INSIDE THE ?debug BLOCK. window.__BIRB is created inside `if (new URLSearchParams(location.search).has('debug'))` at index.html:8927 (HEAD), and EVERY harness loads ?debug=1 — so a workbench built there passes every assertion in CI and is unreachable on a phone at birbmobile.vercel.app, which is the one place it exists to be used. This is the hardwareConcurrency/bloom trap in a new costume: a feature gated on a condition the shipping device never satisfies has not shipped, and the gate passes.
clauses: panel DOM created hidden, unconditionally, outside the ?debug block
gesture listener attached at document level, passive, always
?debug gates ONLY window.__BIRB, exactly as today
at least two independent routes: three-finger hold+release, a keyboard fallback, and a URL flag — and the URL flag MUST NOT be ?debug, or the ruling is defeated by the back door
A1's acceptance requires a page loaded WITHOUT ?debug

three fingers is the first touch count the game can never produce (one is the stick, two is stick+boost / the sprint tracker); must not break the two-finger sprint path (A2), must cancel gameplay pointers on open, must respect touchcancel, must coexist with nipplejs which owns touchZone
production-path obligations: no console.log on the happy path (birb-modes.mjs treats WARNINGS as failures), no per-frame DOM work while closed, no measurable cost when never opened
requirements.stopCondition: G2b: STOP if the gesture registered inside the ?debug block.

requirements.ruling: Precedence is panel request > adaptive tier > capability probe. A panel request is not a suggestion: once Manual is active the adaptive tier must not write the quantities the panel owns, not once and not on the next frame. Every site in the routing register routes through one function. isLowEnd (index.html:3578) stays advisory and supplies defaults only — on iOS Safari navigator.hardwareConcurrency is undefined.
routedSites: updateRendererSize@6787 (T3, becomes the single sizing function)

requirements.ruling: SC-DPR runs before any assertion and exits 1 — not 0, not a skip, not a warning — if tier-0 and tier-1 pixel ratios are equal at the harness context. A dead discriminator must not pass silently. tools/birb-modes.mjs runs at deviceScaleFactor 1, where they ARE equal; the quality harness must not inherit that context and must not be 'fixed' by copying it.

Every field with no source renders its sentinel, and a Wave-2 panel shows the Wave-3 fields AS SENTINELS rather than omitting them — an absent row reads as 'not part of the product', a sentinel reads as 'not measured yet'. TEL-13 (last adjustment/reason), TEL-14 (cooldown) and TEL-15 (active mode) have NO source in Wave 0 and must render the sentinel; deriving 'Manual' from isPinned() is an inference and is forbidden.

telemetry.why: today's sampler emits one averaged rate per 250 ms; percentiles over that are meaningless
no timing brackets exist around the update or submission steps; separate accumulators required

telemetry.forbiddenReason: no-context (that is a wiring bug, and a STOP)

telemetry.source: renderer.info.memory.geometries / .textures — exists on the renderer, not yet exposed
computable from effective().bloom.* (w*h*4 per target) — not computed today
telemetry.label: always 'estimated' — resource counts are not byte-accurate GPU memory readings

telemetry.why: adaptiveTier records state.lastTierChange (a timestamp) and NO reason at all, and neither is exposed. Fabricating it from tier+pinned is forbidden.
MIN_INTERVAL_MS=1500 is a constant inside the IIFE; no REMAINING cooldown is computed, and the constant is not the field.

no mode concept exists; isPinned() is a boolean latch with no unpin. Reporting pinned===true as 'Manual' is an inference and is forbidden — a harness pin and a user's Manual have different exit paths.

deferrals.deferred: Persisted learning store (cross-session profiles in localStorage)
deferrals.reason: Largest new surface in the plan. Its 'coarse capability bucket' will reach for navigator.hardwareConcurrency — this repo's most expensive documented mistake, still live at index.html:3578 — and its benefit is unmeasurable without the device access that gates everything else. Privacy deny-list, entry cap and age-out were assigned by three designs to a module with no test file.
deferrals.reopenedBy: A Wave 4 device session showing a COLD session's first 60 s are materially worse than a warm one's, AND an authored test suite covering deny-list, entry cap and age-out.
deferrals.shipsInstead: In-session action history in memory: predicted vs observed benefit, confidence, failed probes, cooldowns (src/game/perf-learning.js, W3 P3.2). Panel exposes learning on/off and reset over the in-session store.

deferrals.deferred: GPU timer query lifecycle — query pools, deferred multi-frame reads, disjoint handling at scale
deferrals.reason: EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 is exposed by neither Safari nor SwiftShader, so a full implementation ships permanently on its null branch, green, unexercised. A timer around renderer.render() is not GPU execution time anyway.
deferrals.reopenedBy: A phone reporting the extension present AND returning non-disjoint results across a Wave 4 session.
deferrals.shipsInstead: The probe only: feature-detect and report { state, reason } from the closed enum. reason 'no-context' is a STOP (wiring bug); 'no-extension' is a platform fact. The bounded-probe fallback is NOT deferred — it has to work anyway and is what will actually run.

deferrals.deferred: The 30 FPS target-rate row, with real render pacing
deferrals.reason: docs/CUTTING_EDGE_2026.md records that iOS caps rAF at 60 Hz. Half-rate skipping on a 60 Hz panel produces judder that scores WORSE on the very interval statistics this plan adopts (p95, >25ms count). Shipping it as a menu entry that makes the measured tail worse is an anti-feature.
deferrals.reopenedBy: A NAMED pacing mechanism plus device evidence that a 30 FPS profile improves p95/p99 and sustained thermals on the same route.
deferrals.shipsInstead: Nothing. Target rate ships 60 only; the row is ABSENT from the panel, not present-and-disabled. 90/120 likewise deferred.

deferrals.deferred: The 'richer experimental surface detail' shader variant (CTL-6's third option)
deferrals.reason: Uncommissioned shader authorship whose only oracle is a human looking at a contact sheet — in a repo that shipped TWO whole systems invisible because a shader failed to compile at exit zero (the weather's `half`, reserved in GLSL ES; the city ground's doubly-declared varying).
deferrals.reopenedBy: A device-measured headroom figure from Wave 4 large enough to state as its budget, AND tools/birb-shaders.mjs green on the variant. Commissioned one at a time in Wave 6.
deferrals.shipsInstead: Surface detail ships baseline / simplified only.

deferrals.deferred: Anti-laundering meta-infrastructure: held-out fixture directories materialised outside the worktree, sha256 oracle manifests as a product, maintained mutation catalogues
deferrals.reason: Two designs proposed building a second product alongside the first.
deferrals.reopenedBy: Evidence that a cheap-tier agent actually laundered an oracle past G1 — i.e. the cheap rule below demonstrably failing.
deferrals.shipsInstead: One cheap rule: implementation tasks land on a branch where tests/** and tools/*.mjs are read-only, and every oracle addresses a test FILE PATH (R1, R5). G1's flip test supplies the discrimination proof the mutation catalogue was going to.

deferrals.reason: No mechanism for any of them exists anywhere in the repo, and each needs a device-measured headroom figure as its stated budget.
deferrals.reopenedBy: Wave 4 evidence + G5 pass. Wave 6, one at a time.
deferrals.shipsInstead: Experiments 1 and 5 only — the two buildable from what exists; 5 is the one evidence class that survives software rendering.

deferrals.reason: Already measured and rejected: draw calls rose past the 100 budget for a 17-22% triangle saving, because this world's props are deliberately scattered evenly and sector culling only rejects the far hemisphere.
deferrals.reopenedBy: A CHANGED SCENE DISTRIBUTION plus new evidence. Not reopened by 'we have a workbench now'.
deferrals.shipsInstead: Nothing. Do not rebuild it blind.

names._comment: R7 — one harness, one panel, one controller. Five designs independently proposed four different harnesses for the one check the plan asks for once.

compatibilityProfile.rule: The new controller ships with a profile that reproduces today's 55/58 three-tier behaviour EXACTLY. The new policy is reachable only from the panel and a URL flag, and the switchover is gated on a recorded device session.
compatibilityProfile.why: A no-device outcome then ships a workbench and a measurement rig — genuinely valuable, fully verifiable in CI — and nothing riskier than today.
compatibilityProfile.measuredBy: tools/birb-perf-ab.mjs: Auto vs this reference profile vs fixed profiles. The only check that answers whether any of this was worth building.

ciNote.risk: Already runs four browser commands after a Chromium install. Adding birb-quality.mjs without raising the timeout converts a real failure into a timeout, which reads as flake.
